# mcp server

Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server for the *@trycompai/mcp-server* API.

## 中文说明

Mcp Server 是 Claude Code 的能力扩展，用来处理对应领域里的文件、网页、数据或自动化流程。

## 典型场景
- 使用 Mcp Server 完成相关任务
- 减少手工复制、整理和重复操作
- 把固定流程交给 Claude Code 执行

overlay: 1.0.0
info:
  title: CompAI MCP — force presigned uploads
  version: 1.0.0
# =============================================================================
# WHY THIS OVERLAY EXISTS (read before editing the questionnaire upload tools)
# =============================================================================
# Agent / LLM clients (our MCP server) must NEVER receive file bytes inline.
# Sending a file as base64 in a tool argument forces the model to emit the whole
# file token-by-token — catastrophically slow, token-expensive, and it overflows
# the context window. (We hit this twice in testing.)
#
# This overlay strips every "hand me the raw file" input from the MCP tool
# surface so the model is FORCED down the presigned-upload path:
#
#     create-upload-url(purpose=questionnaire)  ->  { uploadUrl, s3Key }
#     PUT raw bytes to uploadUrl                 ->  (straight to S3)
#     upload-and-parse(s3Key)                    ->  parse + answer
#
# IMPORTANT: this overlay is applied ONLY during Speakeasy generation (it is
# wired into .speakeasy/workflow.yaml). The source spec
# packages/docs/openapi.json is left untouched, so the public API docs and the
# web UI keep their base64 / multipart upload paths — browsers handle binary
# natively and should not be forced through presign.
#
# When a NEW feature starts accepting agent uploads, follow the same recipe:
# remove its inline-file field here and add an `s3Key` to its DTO instead.
# =============================================================================
actions:
  # 1. Drop the base64 `fileData` field from the questionnaire JSON upload tool,
  #    leaving `s3Key` as the only way an MCP client can supply a file.
  - target: "$.components.schemas.UploadAndParseDto.properties.fileData"
    remove: true

  # 1b. Rewrite the `s3Key` description for the MCP tool. The source description
  #     references `fileData` ("provide exactly one of..."), which is correct for
  #     the public API/docs but dangling here — MCP clients can't see fileData
  #     (we removed it above). Give agents the explicit upload recipe instead.
  - target: "$.components.schemas.UploadAndParseDto.properties.s3Key"
    update:
      description: >-
        The questionnaire file to parse. First call create-upload-url with
        purpose=questionnaire to get a presigned URL and s3Key, PUT the raw file
        bytes to that URL, then pass the returned s3Key here. This is the only
        way to supply a file — never send file contents inline.

  # 2-4. Disable the multipart "/upload" tools for MCP. Each accepts a binary
  #    `file` an agent could only populate by base64-ing it — the exact
  #    anti-pattern above. They are redundant for agents: the presigned flow
  #    plus their JSON siblings (which operate on an already-uploaded
  #    questionnaire by id) cover the same capability. The HTTP endpoints stay
  #    live for the web UI / direct callers; only the MCP tools are removed.
  - target: "$.paths['/v1/questionnaire/upload-and-parse/upload'].post"
    update:
      x-speakeasy-mcp:
        disabled: true
  - target: "$.paths['/v1/questionnaire/parse/upload'].post"
    update:
      x-speakeasy-mcp:
        disabled: true
  - target: "$.paths['/v1/questionnaire/answers/export/upload'].post"
    update:
      x-speakeasy-mcp:
        disabled: true

  # 5-6. Disable the two answer-generation tools that can't work over MCP:
  #   - /v1/questionnaire/auto-answer streams Server-Sent Events; a single
  #     JSON-RPC tool call can't consume an SSE stream.
  #   - /v1/questionnaire/answers/export returns a binary file (pdf/csv/xlsx);
  #     an agent can't render that inline in chat.
  #   Agents should instead use POST /v1/questionnaire/{id}/auto-answer (returns
  #   JSON, runs in the background) and poll GET /v1/questionnaire/{id} for the
  #   answers. Both HTTP endpoints stay live for the web UI.
  - target: "$.paths['/v1/questionnaire/auto-answer'].post"
    update:
      x-speakeasy-mcp:
        disabled: true
  - target: "$.paths['/v1/questionnaire/answers/export'].post"
    update:
      x-speakeasy-mcp:
        disabled: true

  # 7-9. Force presigned uploads for task attachments, knowledge-base documents,
  #   and offboarding evidence — same reason as the questionnaire tools above:
  #   base64 through an LLM is impractically slow and times out (customer-reported).
  #   Strip the inline base64 `fileData` from the MCP tool surface so agents must
  #   use create-upload-url (purpose=attachment|document|evidence) -> PUT to S3 ->
  #   pass the returned `s3Key`. The base spec keeps `fileData` for the web UI /
  #   direct callers; only the MCP tools lose it.
  - target: "$.components.schemas.UploadAttachmentDto.properties.fileData"
    remove: true
  - target: "$.components.schemas.UploadDocumentDto.properties.fileData"
    remove: true
  - target: "$.components.schemas.CompleteChecklistItemDto.properties.fileData"
    remove: true

  # 10-11. Disable the automation-authoring tools for MCP. Creating a working
  #   automation requires generating its evidence-collection SCRIPT, and that
  #   step lives ONLY in the enterprise-api browser chat (an AI tool writes the
  #   .draft.js to S3, then publish copies it to .vN.js). Neither the public API
  #   nor MCP can produce that script. So over MCP these two POSTs only ever
  #   create an empty automation shell + a version row pointing at a script that
  #   was never generated — a dead end that confuses agents. Hide them until the
  #   script-generation step is exposed as a first-class (async) endpoint.
  #   The HTTP endpoints stay live for the web UI, which drives the full flow.
  #   Read/list/update automation tools remain available over MCP.
  - target: "$.paths['/v1/tasks/{taskId}/automations'].post"
    update:
      x-speakeasy-mcp:
        disabled: true
  - target: "$.paths['/v1/tasks/{taskId}/automations/{automationId}/versions'].post"
    update:
      x-speakeasy-mcp:
        disabled: true

## Installation

<summary>Claude Desktop</summary>

Install the MCP server as a Desktop Extension using the pre-built [`mcp-server.mcpb`](https://github.com/trycompai/comp/releases/download/v0.2.3/mcp-server.mcpb) file:

Simply drag and drop the [`mcp-server.mcpb`](https://github.com/trycompai/comp/releases/download/v0.2.3/mcp-server.mcpb) file onto Claude Desktop to install the extension.

The MCP bundle package includes the MCP server and all necessary configuration. Once installed, the server will be available without additional setup.

> [!NOTE]
> MCP bundles provide a streamlined way to package and distribute MCP servers. Learn more about [Desktop Extensions](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/desktop-extensions).

<!-- Start Progressive Discovery [dynamic-mode] -->
## Progressive Discovery

MCP servers with many tools can bloat LLM context windows, leading to increased token usage and tool confusion. Dynamic mode solves this by exposing only a small set of meta-tools that let agents progressively discover and invoke tools on demand.

To enable dynamic mode, pass the `--mode dynamic` flag when starting your server:

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "CompAi": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@trycompai/mcp-server", "start", "--mode", "dynamic"],
      // ... other server arguments
    }
  }
}
```

In dynamic mode, the server registers only the following meta-tools instead of every individual tool:

- **`list_tools`**: Lists all available tools with their names and descriptions.
- **`describe_tool_input`**: Returns the input schema for one or more tools by name.
- **`execute_tool`**: Executes a tool by name with its arguments.

This approach significantly reduces the number of tokens sent to the LLM on each request, which is especially useful for servers with a large number of tools.
<!-- End Progressive Discovery [dynamic-mode] -->

## Development

Run locally without a published npm package:
1. Clone this repository
2. Run `npm install`
3. Run `npm run build`
4. Run `node ./bin/mcp-server.js start --apikey `
To use this local version with Cursor, Claude or other MCP Clients, you'll need to add the following config:

```json
{
  "command": "node",
  "args": [
    "./bin/mcp-server.js",
    "start",
    "--apikey",
    ""
  ]
}
```

Or to debug the MCP server locally, use the official MCP Inspector: 

```bash
npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector node ./bin/mcp-server.js start --apikey 
```



## Publishing to Anthropic MCP Registry

This server generates a `server.json` that conforms to the [official MCP Registry schema](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/registry/about). You can publish automatically via your Speakeasy workflow or manually using the `mcp-publisher` CLI.

### Automated Publishing (Recommended)

Add `mcpRegistry` to the `publish` block in your `workflow.yaml`:

```yaml
targets:
  my-mcp:
    target: mcp-typescript
    source: my-source
    publish:
      npm:
        token: $NPM_TOKEN
      mcpRegistry:
        auth: github-oidc  # recommended, no token needed
```

The `github-oidc` method uses GitHub Actions OIDC — no secrets required. For other auth methods:
- `github` — requires a `MCP_REGISTRY_TOKEN` secret (GitHub PAT with `read:org` + `read:user` scopes)
- `dns` — requires a `MCP_REGISTRY_TOKEN` secret (Ed25519 private key for custom domain namespaces)

When the Speakeasy workflow runs, it will automatically publish to npm first, then to the MCP Registry.

### Manual Publishing

If you prefer to publish manually, follow the [official publishing guide](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/blob/main/docs/guides/publishing/publish-server.md):

1. **Publish to npm**: `npm publish --access public`
2. **Install the publisher CLI**:
   ```bash
   curl -sL "https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/releases/latest/download/mcp-publisher_$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')_$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/').tar.gz" | tar xz mcp-publisher && sudo mv mcp-publisher /usr/local/bin/
   ```
3. **Authenticate** (GitHub OAuth for `io.github.*` namespaces):
   ```bash
   mcp-publisher login github
   ```
4. **Publish**: `mcp-publisher publish`
5. **Verify**:
   ```bash
   curl "https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=<your-mcp-name>"
   ```

## Contributions

While we value contributions to this MCP Server, the code is generated programmatically. Any manual changes added to internal files will be overwritten on the next generation. 
We look forward to hearing your feedback. Feel free to open a PR or an issue with a proof of concept and we'll do our best to include it in a future release.
